why: A = corollary_3_4_3 ∧ corollary_3_4_3_isConjugate ∧ compIso_eq_strongShift ∧ four general strong-bundle-isomorphism lemmas (no universe parameters). A ⇒ B fails at the hypotheses: A's corollary assumes g and s sc-smooth on the relatively open U (set sense), B only that s is an sc-smooth germ (IsScSmoothGerm G s, level-dependent neighbourhoods) and that Φ_* g is a basic germ (so g is only a germ); a germ does not give set-sense sc-smoothness on any U₀ ∋ 0, so A cannot be applied (B's Φ, U', G', Φ_* g do form the project's ConjugationData, conj holding on all of U). Even under set-sense hypotheses, B wants Fin n'/Fin N' parameter spaces and a level-0 Ψ, while A's Λ₀ = linIso₀ lands in paramProd (Pn × Cs) XB, needing a transport of basic germs along linear isomorphisms (glue, not attempted). B ⇒ A fails: A's lemmas (shift, comp, pushforward_comp, prodMap, linIso) are general facts about strong bundle isomorphisms not implied by B, and A's corollary is for arbitrary finite-dimensional parameter types.
